definition: Amália is a Portuguese large language model (LLM) announced in November 2024 by the Portuguese Prime-Minister Luís Montenegro.
details: Its final version is expected to be launched in 2026. It is being developed by Center for Responsible AI (Centro para a AI Responsável) and by the research centers of NOVA School of Science and Technology and Instituto Superior Técnico.

explainer.lead: Amália is a Portuguese large language model built around European Portuguese, cultural representation and data protection. It is intended for Portuguese public administration, with a final open version expected in 2026.

tiers.eli5: Amália is like a computer pen pal being taught to speak the Portuguese used in Portugal and to understand local culture. Its makers also say protecting people's data is a key part of the project. A test version is available only to public administration, while the finished version is expected to be shared openly in 2026.
tiers.practitioner: Engineering use during the September 2025 beta is confined to Portuguese Public Administration, so outside teams cannot treat it as a generally available model. Evaluation should focus on European Portuguese output, cultural representation and data protection, the three priorities identified by Center for Responsible AI CEO Paulo Dimas. The planned open final version is expected in 2026.
tiers.paperLevel: Amália := a Portuguese large language model whose stated project priorities are the European Portuguese linguistic variant, cultural representation and data protection. It entered beta in 2025, with the September beta restricted to Public Administration. The final model is expected to be open and launched in 2026.

usedIn.name: Portuguese Public Administration
usedIn.detail: The September 2025 beta is available only to Public Administration, following the 2024 announcement that the Agency for Administrative Modernization would bring the model into its work.

flow: The Center for Responsible AI and research centers at NOVA School of Science and Technology and Instituto Superior Técnico develop the model.
The September 2025 beta is released exclusively to Public Administration.
The final version is expected to launch as an open model in 2026.
explainer.origin: Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro announced Amália in November 2024. Paulo Dimas, CEO of the Center for Responsible AI, identified European Portuguese, cultural representation and data protection as the project's three fundamental points.
explainer.lineage: An improved version was anticipated when the beta phase was announced in April 2025, followed by the restricted September beta. An October website announcement reiterated that the final version would be open, with launch expected in 2026.
explainer.whyItMatters: Amália explicitly treats the Portuguese used in Portugal, local cultural representation and data protection as central design priorities. Its public-administration deployment and planned open release make those priorities relevant beyond a research prototype.
